If energy release in the formation of four bonds is more than energy absorbed in promotion of s-electron then hybridization is feasible. This happens in case of C and Si and also for Ge in most cases. However, Sn and Pb form weak covalent bonds due to their larger atomic radius. So, the energy released in the formation of four covalent bonds may be less than the energy needed to promote s-electrons. So, hybridization will not occur and two s-electrons remain paired. They are called inert pair and effect is called inert pair effect, thus, Sn and Pb show oxidation state of +2 in addition to +4.

13.4.4.2 Inert Pair Effect and the Formation of Covalent Bonds

Carbon normally forms four covalent bonds rather than two. The outer electronic structure of carbon is,

There are two unpaired electrons in 2px and 2py orbitals. In order to form bonds, however, carbon promotes one ‘s’ electron to the empty 2pz orbital.

This produces 4 unpaired electrons which (after hybridization) can form four covalent bonds. To promote the ‘s’ electron to ‘p’ orbital requires energy. During the covalent bond formation each bond releases energy and this energy is enough for the promotion of ‘s’ electron to ‘p’ orbital.

The other members of Group – IVA, such as lead show reluctance to do the same; this is due the decrease in bond energies down the group. Bond energies decreases as atomic size increases and the bonding pair move away from the two nuclei and also because of screening effect. For example, the energy released by two extra Pb–Cl bonds may not be enough to cater the extra energy needed to promote a 6s electron into the empty 6p orbital.

13.4.5 Chlorides of Carbon, Silicon and Lead

Carbon, silicon and lead give tetrachlorides, which are simple covalent molecules. They exist in liquid state at room temperature with the general formula of MCl₄. (where M = C, Si, Pb).

13.4.5.1 Structures and Stability

i. Structure

The MCl₄ have a tetrahedral shape with a bond angle of 109.5°. A typical example is carbon tetrachloride.

Figure 13.3 Structure of CCl₄.

ii. Stability

When we move down the Group, compounds with a +2 oxidation state in Group – IVA element become more stable.

This means that the +4 oxidation is less favourable while the +2 oxidation state is more favourable down the Group.

Thus, stability decreases from CCl₄ to PbCl₄. Lead tetrachloride (PbCl₄) at room temperature, tends to decompose to give lead dichloride (PbCl₂) and chlorine gas.

PbCl₄(s) → PbCl₂(s) + Cl₂(g)

13.4.5.2 Reactions with Water

Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄) does not react with water. This is due to bulky nature of chlorine atoms around small carbon atom. As a result, oxygen of water cannot penetrate to reach carbon atom.

SiCl₄ to PbCl₄ react violently with water to produce their respective oxides and fumes of HCl.

13.4.5 د کاربن، سیلیکان او سرب کلورایډونه

کاربن، سیلیکان او سرب ټېټراکلورایډونه جوړوي، چې ساده کووالنټ مالیکولونه دي. هغوی د خونې په تودوخه کې په مایع حالت کې وي او عمومي فورمول یې MCl₄ دی (چې M = C، Si، Pb دی).

13.4.5.1 جوړښتونه او ثبات

i. جوړښت

MCl₄ څلورمخیز شکل لري او د تړون زاویه یې 109.5° ده. کاربن ټېټراکلورایډ یې یوه عادي بېلګه ده.

شکل 13.3 د CCl₄ جوړښت.

ii. ثبات

په ګروپ کې ښکته تګ سره د IVA ګروپ د عنصر د +2 د اکسیدېشن حالت لرونکي مرکبات ډېر ثابت کېږي.

دا مانا لري چې په ګروپ کې ښکته +4 اکسیدېشن لږ مساعد دی، خو +2 د اکسیدېشن حالت ډېر مساعد دی.

نو له CCl₄ څخه PbCl₄ ته ثبات کمېږي. سرب ټېټراکلورایډ (PbCl₄) د خونې په تودوخه کې د تجزیې تمایل لري او سرب ډای کلورایډ (PbCl₂) او کلورین ګاز جوړوي.

PbCl₄(s) → PbCl₂(s) + Cl₂(g)

13.4.5.2 له اوبو سره تعاملونه

کاربن ټېټراکلورایډ (CCl₄) له اوبو سره تعامل نه کوي. دا د کوچني کاربن اټوم شاوخوا د کلورین د اټومونو د لویې اندازې له امله دی. په پایله کې د اوبو اکسیجن دننه نه شي ننوتلای چې کاربن اټوم ته ورسېږي.

له SiCl₄ څخه تر PbCl₄ پورې له اوبو سره په شدت تعامل کوي او خپل اړوند اکسایډونه او د HCl لوګي جوړوي.

i. Promotion of one electron of the s-orbital into higher energy p-orbital. Energy must be provided for this process.

ii. Formation of four covalent bonds by the four hybrid orbitals, energy is released in this process.

If energy release in the formation of four bonds is more than energy absorbed in promotion of s-electron then hybridization is feasible. This happens in case of C and Si and also for Ge in most cases. However, Sn and Pb form weak covalent bonds due to their larger atomic radius. So, the energy released in the formation of four covalent bonds may be less than the energy needed to promote s-electrons. So, hybridization will not occur and two s-electrons remain paired. They are called inert pair and effect is called inert pair effect, thus, Sn and Pb show oxidation state of +2 in addition to +4.

13.4.4.2 Inert Pair Effect and the Formation of Covalent Bonds

Carbon normally forms four covalent bonds rather than two. The outer electronic structure of carbon is,

There are two unpaired electrons in 2px and 2py orbitals. In order to form bonds, however, carbon promotes one ‘s’ electron to the empty 2pz orbital.

This produces 4 unpaired electrons which (after hybridization) can form four covalent bonds. To promote the ‘s’ electron to ‘p’ orbital requires energy. During the covalent bond formation each bond releases energy and this energy is enough for the promotion of ‘s’ electron to ‘p’ orbital.

The other members of Group – IVA, such as lead show reluctance to do the same; this is due the decrease in bond energies down the group. Bond energies decreases as atomic size increases and the bonding pair move away from the two nuclei and also because of screening effect. For example, the energy released by two extra Pb–Cl bonds may not be enough to cater the extra energy needed to promote a 6s electron into the empty 6p orbital.

13.4.5 Chlorides of Carbon, Silicon and Lead

Carbon, silicon and lead give tetrachlorides, which are simple covalent molecules. They exist in liquid state at room temperature with the general formula of MCl₄. (where M = C, Si, Pb).

13.4.5.1 Structures and Stability

i. Structure

The MCl₄ have a tetrahedral shape with a bond angle of 109.5°. A typical example is carbon tetrachloride.

Figure 13.3 Structure of CCl₄.

ii. Stability

When we move down the Group, compounds with a +2 oxidation state in Group – IVA element become more stable.

This means that the +4 oxidation is less favourable while the +2 oxidation state is more favourable down the Group.

Thus, stability decreases from CCl₄ to PbCl₄. Lead tetrachloride (PbCl₄) at room temperature, tends to decompose to give lead dichloride (PbCl₂) and chlorine gas.

PbCl₄(s) → PbCl₂(s) + Cl₂(g)

13.4.5.2 Reactions with Water

Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄) does not react with water. This is due to bulky nature of chlorine atoms around small carbon atom. As a result, oxygen of water cannot penetrate to reach carbon atom.

SiCl₄ to PbCl₄ react violently with water to produce their respective oxides and fumes of HCl.
